release_date.notes: System card dated May 28 2026; Bedrock GA announced same day.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Docs list reliable knowledge cutoff as Jan 2026 and training data cutoff as Jan 2026.

context_window_tokens.notes: 1M token context window on Claude API, Bedrock, and Vertex AI. On Microsoft Foundry the window is 200k tokens. Standard pricing applies across the full 1M window (no surcharge for long context).

input_output_shared.notes: Input + output draw from one shared pool. Context window = all text the model attends to including its own response.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived: context_window (1M) minus max_output (128k). Anthropic documents max_input via the Models API; no static hard number in prose docs. Practical limit slightly lower due to tool-use system prompt overhead.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: 128k output tokens on synchronous Messages API.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: 300k output via Message Batches API with beta header output-300k-2026-03-24. Standard sync API cap is 128k.

extended_context.notes: No separate extended context beta needed; 1M token window is the default GA window for Opus 4.8. The 1M window is fully included at standard per-token pricing.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Thinking budget tokens are a subset of max_tokens and are billed as output tokens. Previous turn thinking blocks are automatically stripped by the API and do not accumulate as input. Opus 4.8 supports adaptive thinking (always on).

tokenizer_family.notes: Anthropic uses a proprietary BPE tokenizer. Opus 4.7 and later use a new tokenizer that may use up to 35% more tokens than models before Opus 4.7 for the same fixed text. This newer tokenizer applies to Opus 4.8. Not the same family as cl100k or o200k.

tokenizer_public.notes: Anthropic has not released the tokenizer weights. Exact counts require calling the count_tokens API endpoint.

tokenizer_access.notes: POST /v1/messages/count_tokens. Accepts the same structured inputs as /v1/messages (system prompts, tools, images, PDFs). Free to call, subject to RPM rate limits per usage tier.

count_tokens_method.value: POST /v1/messages/count_tokens with model='claude-opus-4-8'
count_tokens_method.notes: Returns {input_tokens: N}. Counts include tool definitions, system prompts, images, PDFs. Count is an estimate; actual billed tokens may differ slightly. System-added tokens are counted but not billed. Always use model-specific endpoint since tokenizers differ across model generations.

image_token_rule.value: ceil(width/28) x ceil(height/28) visual tokens per image; max 4784 tokens for Opus 4.8 (high-res, max 2576px long edge). Images billed at same input token rate.
image_token_rule.notes: Opus 4.7+ has high-resolution support: max 2576px long edge, up to 4784 visual tokens vs 1568 on older models. Images padded to next multiple of 28px on bottom/right.

audio_token_rule.notes: Audio input is not supported on any current Claude model as of 2026-06-21. All models support text and image input.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Anthropic pricing FAQ states ~4 chars per token for English. Newer tokenizer (Opus 4.7+) produces ~35% more tokens for same text, implying ~3.5 chars/token for Opus 4.8. Use count_tokens API for accuracy; this rough estimate is for raw_json_rough fallback only.

native_mcp.notes: MCP connector (beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20) supported on Claude API and Claude Platform on AWS. Not yet available on Amazon Bedrock or Vertex AI. Supports remote HTTP MCP servers (Streamable HTTP and SSE). Only tool calls supported from MCP spec (not prompts/resources).

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Claude can emit multiple tool_use blocks in a single assistant turn.

max_tools_hard.notes: No documented API-enforced hard limit on number of tools per request (unlike OpenAI's 128-tool cap). Tool search doc explicitly documents up to 10,000 tools in a catalog when using defer_loading. Anthropic has not published a per-request numeric count cap in prose docs as of 2026-06-21.

max_tools_practical.notes: Tool search docs note accuracy degrades past 30-50 tools without deferred loading. Anthropic engineering posts confirm the 30-50 tool cliff. Claude Desktop community reports ~100 tool limit in practice. With tool search / defer_loading the practical catalog can extend to thousands.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Tools defined as {name, description, input_schema (JSON Schema)} in the tools[] parameter. Tool name must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$. Tool definitions are serialised into a special system prompt injected by the API. MCP tools surface via mcp_toolset objects and count identically as input tokens.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Explicitly documented: tool names, descriptions, and schemas in the tools parameter are billed as input tokens. Additionally, a tool-use system prompt is automatically injected: Opus 4.8 adds 290 tokens (auto/none tool choice) or 410 tokens (any/tool choice). Each tool definition's JSON also adds tokens proportional to its size.

tool_search_deferral.notes: defer_loading:true on any tool definition keeps it out of the context until Claude searches for and discovers it via the tool_search_tool. Two variants: regex (tool_search_tool_regex_20251119) and BM25 (tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119). Catalog up to 10,000 tools. Reduces context by >85% in multi-server setups. Compatible with prompt caching and strict mode. Supported on Haiku 4.5+, Sonnet 4.0+, Opus 4.0+.

max_tool_name_len.notes: Tool name must match regex ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$. Skill names have a separate 64-character limit.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented character or token cap on tool description length as of 2026-06-21. Anthropic's best-practices guidance recommends at least 3-4 sentences per description; long descriptions consume input tokens proportionally. Effectively bounded by the total request payload limit (32 MB) and context window.

max_request_size.notes: Direct Claude API (api.anthropic.com) enforces a 32 MB max request payload size. Partner platforms differ: Vertex AI limits to 30 MB, Amazon Bedrock to 20 MB. Tool definitions count toward this payload alongside message content — two separate ceilings apply (payload bytes and context window tokens).

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-tool-result byte or token cap as of 2026-06-21. Tool result content blocks (text, image, document) count as input tokens and are bounded by the 32 MB request limit and the model's context window. The handle-tool-calls doc notes that tool results often carry untrusted third-party content. Bloated results waste context and should be filtered at the application layer.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel tool use is supported (Claude emits multiple tool_use blocks per turn) but no fixed numeric cap on simultaneous calls per turn is published. In practice bounded by the model's output token budget for that turn. disable_parallel_tool_use flag available to opt out.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No specific tool-use-per-turn numeric limit published in Anthropic docs as of 2026-06-21. The phrase 'Claude reached its tool-use limit for this turn' appears in community reports for claude.ai (consumer product client-side cap) but is not documented with a specific number in the API docs. The task budgets feature (beta) provides an advisory token budget across an agentic loop but is not a tool-call count cap. API users control turn termination via max_tokens and stop_reason.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented hard cap on connected MCP servers in the Claude API (mcp_servers array). The MCP connector API enforces that each mcp_server_name must be referenced by exactly one MCPToolset, but allows multiple servers per request. Claude Code docs say it can connect to 'hundreds' of servers without publishing a fixed cap. Claude Desktop's cap is not published in official docs; community reports suggest ~100 tools aggregate (not server count) before selection accuracy degrades.

max_total_tools.notes: AGGREGATE ceiling across ALL connected servers + built-in tools (NOT a per-server cap), and conditional on tool search / defer_loading. Documented maximum catalog size with defer_loading tool search: 10,000 tools. Without defer_loading the practical effective limit is ~30-50 tools before selection accuracy degrades (Tier-4 empirical). Claude Desktop aggregate tool display cap is reported at ~100 by community (Tier-4) but not documented officially.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Input JSON Schema for tools: supported schema keywords include type, properties, required, description, enum, anyOf, items, and most standard JSON Schema draft-07 keywords. The 'pattern' keyword is explicitly NOT supported when strict:true is used (returns 400 error). No documented maximum nesting depth, maximum properties count, or maximum total schema size. MCP toolset tools count identically to client tools as input tokens. Prompt caching can be applied to the tools parameter via cache_control on an mcp_toolset or individual tool definitions to cache repeated tool schemas at 0.1x input price after a cache write. The input_examples field (optional) adds ~20-200 tokens per tool. Strict mode (strict:true) enables schema-conformant tool calls and composes with defer_loading without grammar recompilation.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: MCP connector (API layer): only HTTP(S) URLs supported for mcp_servers (no local stdio). Each MCP server name must be referenced by exactly one MCPToolset; every declared server must be used. Only tool calls from the MCP spec supported (prompts and resources not yet supported). Tool search regex variant: max 200-character pattern; error codes include too_many_requests, invalid_pattern, pattern_too_long, unavailable. Files API: 500 MB per file, 500 GB per org; file-related API calls limited to ~100 RPM during beta. Request rate limits are tier-based (RPM + ITPM); cached input tokens do not count toward ITPM for most models. Task budgets (beta): advisory token budget spanning agentic loop; minimum 20,000 tokens; supported on Opus 4.8 and Opus 4.7 only (not Sonnet 4.6 or Haiku 4.5). Max request size 32 MB (direct API), 30 MB (Vertex AI), 20 MB (Bedrock).

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

skills_loading_model.notes: Level 1 metadata (~100 tokens per skill) always present in system prompt. Level 2 instructions (<5k tokens from SKILL.md body) loaded on demand via bash when skill is triggered. Level 3 bundled files/scripts loaded as needed via bash without entering context at all (only output enters context).

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: At startup: ~100 tokens per installed skill (name+description YAML frontmatter) injected into system prompt. When triggered: Claude reads SKILL.md via bash, adding up to ~5k tokens of instructions to the context window. Additional bundled files read individually as needed. Scripts run via bash — script code itself never enters context, only stdout/stderr output does. Net effect: a large skill library has minimal startup footprint; only active skills consume meaningful context.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: Tool-use system prompt overhead per request: 290 tokens (tool_choice auto/none), 410 tokens (tool_choice any/tool) for Opus 4.8. Context-awareness tokens injected at turn start (budget tag ~10 tokens) plus system_warning after each tool call (~20 tokens). Not billed — system-added tokens are counted but not charged.

prompt_caching.notes: Two cache durations: 5-minute (1.25x write, 0.1x read) and 1-hour (2x write, 0.1x read). Cache reads = 10% of base input price. Can be applied to tools, system prompts, and conversation history via cache_control. Deferred tool definitions preserve the cached prefix since they are not in the system-prompt prefix. Cache invalidated by any change to the cached prefix content.

memory_feature.notes: First-party memory tool available as a server tool. Persists facts across sessions in a structured store; relevant facts are injected into context as input tokens at the start of sessions. Does not auto-grow context unboundedly; operator controls what is retrieved.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cache read (hit) price = 0.1x base input = $0.50/MTok. Cache write (5-min) = 1.25x = $6.25/MTok. Cache write (1-hr) = 2x = $10/MTok.

batch_discount.notes: Batch API: $2.50/MTok input, $12.50/MTok output. Batch and prompt caching discounts stack.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Images billed as input tokens at the visual-token rate (ceil(w/28)*ceil(h/28) tokens per image, max 4784 for Opus 4.8). No separate per-image fee. PDFs treated similarly. Audio not supported. Server tools may add per-use charges (e.g. web search $10/1k searches).

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Thinking/reasoning tokens (thinking budget) count against max_tokens and are billed at the output token rate ($25/MTok for Opus 4.8). Previous-turn thinking blocks are stripped before billing for subsequent turns.

detail.notes: Opus 4.8 is Anthropic's most capable currently-GA Opus model (May 2026). The effort parameter defaults to high on all surfaces. Fast mode (research preview) available at 2.5x speed for $10/$50 per MTok. The newer tokenizer introduced with Opus 4.7 applies here and produces ~35% more tokens than pre-4.7 models for the same text. Adaptive thinking is always on. Extended thinking is not available (adaptive thinking supersedes it). Batch API supports up to 300k output tokens via output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Reliable knowledge cutoff Aug 2025; training data cutoff Jan 2026.

context_window_tokens.notes: 1M token context window. Sonnet 4.6 announcement stated 1M context in beta at launch; models overview confirms 1M GA window. Standard pricing across full 1M.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived: context_window (1M) minus max_output (64k).

max_output_tokens_max.notes: 300k output via Message Batches API with beta header output-300k-2026-03-24. Standard sync API cap is 64k.

extended_context.notes: 1M is the default GA window; no separate extended-context beta needed.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Sonnet 4.6 supports both extended thinking and adaptive thinking. Thinking tokens are billed as output. Previous-turn thinking blocks stripped automatically.

tokenizer_family.notes: Uses same newer tokenizer family as Opus 4.7+ (introduced with Opus 4.7). ~35% more tokens than pre-4.7 models for the same text. Proprietary BPE, not cl100k or o200k.

audio_token_rule.notes: Audio input not supported.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-result cap. Bounded by 32 MB request limit and context window.

Sonnet 4.6 also features context-awareness: it receives token-budget information at conversation start, allowing it to manage context more effectively over long sessions.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Haiku 4.5 not listed in the 300k batch output beta (only Opus 4.8, 4.7, 4.6, Sonnet 4.6). Max output is 64k on both sync and batch API.

The exact tokenizer generation for Haiku 4.5 is not explicitly documented; it may use the pre-4.7 tokenizer (~4 chars/token). Use count_tokens API for accuracy.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented cap. Same as Opus 4.8. Proportionally more expensive on 200k window.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-result cap. On 200k window, oversized tool results are especially costly as a % of available context.

Level 2 instruction load (~5k tokens when triggered) is correspondingly more significant. Recommend limiting simultaneously-loaded skills to preserve headroom.

detail.notes: Haiku 4.5 is Anthropic's fastest, most cost-efficient model with near-frontier intelligence. Released Oct 2025. 200k context window (not 1M). Supports extended thinking but NOT adaptive thinking. The smallest practical context window among current GA Claude models makes tool/skill footprint management especially important. API model ID is claude-haiku-4-5 (alias) or claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (pinned snapshot). Tokenizer generation may differ from Opus 4.7+ new tokenizer — use count_tokens with model='claude-haiku-4-5' for accuracy.

context_window_tokens.notes: Documented as 'Input token limit: 1,048,576'

input_output_shared.notes: Gemini context window is a single shared pool; input + output draw from the 1,048,576 token window. Max output (65,536) is a separate generation cap, not a separate pool.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Google does not document a separate 'default' output cap distinct from the max; the documented limit is 65,536.

extended_context.notes: 1,048,576 (1M) is the standard GA window; no documented beta/extended window beyond this.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Pricing page explicitly labels output price as 'Output price (including thinking tokens)'. Token counting doc confirms thinking tokens appear in thoughts_token_count and are billed at output rate.

tokenizer_family.notes: Proprietary Gemini tokenizer (SentencePiece-based, closed). Token is approximately 4 characters; 100 tokens ~ 60-80 English words.

tokenizer_public.notes: Tokenizer weights are not publicly released; exact counts require the countTokens API.

tokenizer_access.notes: Use client.models.count_tokens() (Python/JS) or REST models.countTokens endpoint to get exact token counts before sending requests.

count_tokens_method.value: client.models.count_tokens(model='gemini-3.5-flash', contents=...) — Python SDK; ai.models.countTokens({model:'gemini-3.5-flash', contents:...}) — JS SDK; or POST /v1beta/models/gemini-3.5-flash:countTokens

image_token_rule.value: Images with both dimensions <=384 pixels = 258 tokens. Larger images are cropped/scaled into 768x768 pixel tiles, each tile = 258 tokens. Gemini 3 models support media_resolution parameter to control max tokens per image/frame.

audio_token_rule.notes: Audio pricing uses a separate rate for input ($1.00/1M audio tokens vs $0.30/1M text tokens standard tier). Video converts at 263 tokens per second.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Gemini docs state: 'a token is equivalent to about 4 characters'. 100 tokens ~ 60-80 English words.

native_mcp.notes: Experimental MCP client in google-genai SDK (Python and JS). Queries list_tools endpoint of MCP servers and exposes tools to model. Only tool calling — resources and prompts not supported. Deep Research API also has MCP support in preview.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Documented as 'parallel function calling' — model can call multiple functions in a single turn.

max_tools_hard.notes: Hard API-enforced limit. Exceeded requests fail immediately with HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT: 'tools[0].function_declarations: [FIELD_INVALID] At most 512 function declarations can be specified.' Confirmed from live error in Gemini CLI issue #19083 (Feb 2026) with model gemini-3-pro-preview. Applies across all functionDeclarations in the tools array. Not yet stated on the official function-calling doc page but is an enforced proto validation constraint.

max_tools_practical.notes: No Gemini-specific empirical limit documented. Official best-practices page recommends keeping active tool set to maximum 10-20 tools for accuracy. General practitioner consensus (~30-50) from Berkeley FCL work applies but not Gemini-specific data available.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Uses functionDeclarations array in a Tool object: {name, description, parameters (JSON Schema subset)}. Shape is similar to OpenAI function but passed as Tool.functionDeclarations[], not tools[].function.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Function declarations are included in the request and billed as input tokens. Use countTokens with the full request (including tools) to measure footprint.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No documented deferred/lazy tool loading mechanism in the Gemini API. Context caching can be used to cache static tool declarations and amortize the input token cost.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No documented character limit for function/tool names in official Gemini API docs. Best practices page states: use descriptive names 'without spaces, periods, or dashes' (use underscores or camelCase). No maximum length stated. This differs from OpenAI's documented 64-char cap.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented maximum character or token cap on function description strings. Descriptions count toward input tokens (1M window limit applies). Best practices: be clear and detailed; provide examples. No hard length cap published.

max_request_size.notes: Inline data (inlineData field in REST): max 100 MB per request payload. PDFs limited to 50 MB via inline method. External URLs: 100 MB per payload. For larger files use Files API (up to 2 GB per file, 20 GB per project, stored 48h). This is the HTTP payload cap; the token window (1M) is a separate, usually-binding ceiling for text+tool payloads.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-function-response size limit in bytes or tokens. Gemini 3 series supports multimodal function responses (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain inline in functionResponse parts). Size of tool results contributes to the shared 1M token context window.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel function calling is supported — model can emit multiple function calls in a single turn. No documented numeric cap on how many may be emitted simultaneously. Results can be returned out of order; the API matches them via the function call id field (Gemini 3 always returns a unique id per function call).

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No documented hard cap on tool-call/result cycles per conversation turn. Compositional (sequential) function calling is supported natively in Gemini 3 models and the Python SDK automatic function calling loops until no more function calls are made. No 'you've reached your tool-use limit' error analogous to Claude's documented per-turn cap.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented limit on number of simultaneous MCP server connections in the experimental google-genai SDK MCP client. Individual OpenAPI operation descriptions are subject to OpenAPI document guidance but no explicit character cap is documented for plugin function descriptions.

max_request_size.notes: PRODUCT LAYER LIMIT (not raw API bytes). The declarative agent architecture doc explicitly documents a 4,096-token limit that 'includes all context and response data' for the plugin scope. This is the plugin I/O token budget (inputs to + outputs from plugins), not the full model context window. Optimize for ~66% (~2,730 tokens) due to overhead from network latency and Microsoft service processing. The 45-second timeout limit also applies (includes network latency and processing time).

max_tool_result_size.notes: The declarative agent architecture doc explicitly states 'Plugin response limit: 25 items'. This is the max number of items a plugin API/MCP response can return to the agent. Grounding record limit is separately documented at 50 items. These are product-layer item-count limits, not byte limits. Token truncation also applies for large item payloads within the 4,096-token window.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Architecture doc states: 'Because Microsoft grounding and calls to external tools happen sequentially, you can’t use chained operations with grounding data or looped operation plans.' Sequential processing means effectively 1 tool call at a time (no parallel calls). Value set to 1 to represent sequential-only constraint.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No published per-turn tool-call cycle limit. The architecture doc documents a 45-second total timeout (includes network latency and processing), which indirectly bounds multi-step tool use. The sequential processing model also limits complex multi-step agentic runs.

max_connected_servers.notes: No published limit on max MCP servers connectable to a single declarative agent. The manifest schema caps actions (plugins/servers) at 10 per agent (see max_total_tools). Each action entry can reference one MCP server or OpenAPI plugin. So the effective max MCP servers per agent is 10 (via the actions array limit).

max_total_tools.notes: Declarative agent manifest schema v1.7 explicitly states: 'The array must contain at least one and no more than 10 objects' for the actions array. Each action is one plugin (MCP server or API plugin). Additionally, conversation_starters array is capped at 12 objects. At runtime, up to 5 plugins are always-injected into the prompt; beyond 5, semantic matching selects which plugins to inject. Plugin functions per plugin: no manifest cap, but quality degrades with >10 functions.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Plugins use either MCP server tool definitions (raw_mcp via mcp.json) or OpenAPI descriptions (openai_function-style via api-plugin manifest). Both are supported.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Architecture doc explicitly states a 4,096-token limit that 'includes all context and response data' for plugin scope. Plugin definitions are injected into the prompt and count against that window.

tool_search_deferral.notes: When agent has >5 plugins, semantic matching is used to defer plugin injection (only matched plugins are injected). Analogous to tool-search/deferral. For <=5 plugins, all are always injected.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: PRODUCT LAYER LIMITS (M365 Copilot declarative agents): (1) Actions per agent: 1-10 (manifest schema v1.7 hard limit). (2) Always-injected plugins: <=5 (beyond 5 uses semantic matching). (3) Functions per plugin: no manifest cap, but quality degrades with >10. (4) Plugin response: 25 items max. (5) Grounding records: 50 items max. (6) Plugin I/O token budget: 4,096 tokens total (including context + response overhead); optimize to ~66% (~2,730 tokens). (7) Turn timeout: 45 seconds (includes network + processing). (8) Sequential processing only (no parallel tool calls). (9) String property limit in manifest: 4,000 chars default; instructions up to 8,000 chars; agent name up to 100 chars; description up to 1,000 chars. (10) Conversation starters: max 12. (11) OpenAPI plugin auth: OAuth2, API key, and no-auth supported.

detail.notes: PRODUCT-LAYER ENTRY: Microsoft 365 Copilot is a product layer over OpenAI GPT-5 family models (and Microsoft Graph grounding). max_tools_hard.notes: CLIENT LAYER LIMIT (VS Code host). A hard cap of 128 tools is enforced at request time in VS Code agent mode. Error message: 'You may not include more than 128 tools in your request.' Confirmed by multiple VS Code GitHub issues (#290356, #13065 on vscode-copilot-release, #251588, #253539). This is a VS Code/Copilot client-level limit, not a model API limit. Workaround: use the tools picker to deselect tools, or enable 'virtual tools' (github.copilot.chat.virtualTools.threshold setting) to automatically group and defer tools above the threshold. The virtual tools feature groups similar tools under stub 'virtual tool' entries so the model can expand them on demand, staying under the 128 limit.

max_tools_practical.notes: GitHub blog (Nov 2025): GitHub trimmed the default built-in toolset from ~40 tools to 13 core tools based on performance benchmarks. The 13-tool core set improved SWE-Lancer and SWEbench-Verified success rates by 2-5 percentage points vs. the full set. The remaining non-core built-in tools are grouped into 4 virtual categories. This is the GitHub-recommended practical toolset size for best performance, not an absolute cap. With MCP servers, total can exceed 13 but quality degrades with too many tools.

max_tool_name_len.notes: Not explicitly documented by GitHub for the Copilot MCP surface. Underlying model limits apply (e.g., OpenAI GPT-5: 64-char tool name limit). GitHub Copilot does not publish a separate tool-name-length constraint.

max_tool_description_len.notes: Not explicitly documented by GitHub for the Copilot MCP surface. MCP tool descriptions are passed through to the underlying model; that model's limits apply. No GitHub Copilot-specific description-length cap published.

max_request_size.notes: Not published by GitHub for the Copilot product surface. The underlying model context window is the binding constraint (model-dependent). Tool definitions count as input tokens against the selected model's context window. Community reports confirm context fills rapidly with many MCP tools loaded.

max_tool_result_size.notes: Not explicitly documented by GitHub for the Copilot MCP surface. Tool results are passed back to the model as input tokens; the model context window is the binding constraint. No separate tool-result-size cap published for GitHub Copilot.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Not documented. Agent mode processes tool calls sequentially in practice; parallel tool calls may be model-dependent. No explicit parallel tool call count cap published for GitHub Copilot.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: Not explicitly documented for GitHub Copilot. The model context window bounds multi-step tool use indirectly. No published per-turn tool-call cycle cap analogous to Claude Code's tool-use limit.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented limit on the number of MCP servers connectable in VS Code. The binding constraint is the 128-tool hard cap (max_tools_hard): across all connected servers, total tools must stay at or below 128 at request time. The virtual tools feature (github.copilot.chat.virtualTools.threshold) mitigates this by deferring excess tools behind stub entries. No per-environment server count cap published.

max_total_tools.unit: tools per request (across all connected MCP servers)
max_total_tools.notes: Same as max_tools_hard: 128 tools is the total cap across all connected MCP servers at request time in VS Code agent mode. Virtual tools feature introduced to manage this: MCP servers with many tools are grouped into virtual tool stubs, reducing effective tool count in the request payload while preserving access to all tools on demand. Setting github.copilot.chat.virtualTools.threshold controls when virtualization kicks in (but capping at 128 total remains).

tool_definition_shape.notes: GitHub Copilot uses the MCP protocol directly. Tool definitions are MCP tool schema objects. The underlying model may re-serialize these to its own format (openai_function for GPT models, anthropic_tool for Claude) internally.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: MCP tool definitions are injected into the model context per turn and consume input tokens. This is the core premise of the MCP Token Footprint tool. GitHub community reports confirm context fills up with large numbers of MCP tools.

tool_search_deferral.notes: Virtual tools feature (GA/rolling out in VS Code): MCP tools are grouped by embedding-guided clustering into virtual tool stubs. The model sees the stub and can expand it to access the actual tools. Controlled by github.copilot.chat.virtualTools.threshold setting. This is effectively deferred/lazy tool loading analogous to ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH in Claude Code. Also: embedding-guided tool routing pre-selects semantically relevant tool groups before model requests, achieving 94.5% tool-use coverage vs 69% for static tool lists.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: CLIENT LAYER LIMITS (GitHub Copilot / VS Code): (1) Hard tool cap: 128 tools per request across all connected MCP servers (VS Code client layer, not model API layer). Error: 'You may not include more than 128 tools in your request.' (2) Default built-in toolset: trimmed from ~40 to 13 core tools in Nov 2025 rollout; remaining grouped into 4 virtual categories. (3) Virtual tools: github.copilot.chat.virtualTools.threshold setting groups large MCP server tool sets into stub virtual tools to stay under the 128 limit. (4) All configured MCP tools loaded into context per session (always-on before virtual tools). (5) Tool definitions consume input tokens against selected model's context window. (6) No published tool-name or tool-description length cap at GitHub Copilot product layer; underlying model caps apply.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Multi-model surface: tool limits are at the VS Code/Copilot client layer (128-tool cap); underlying model API limits (e.g., OpenAI 128, Claude no fixed per-request cap but 10k aggregate catalog) also apply and the more restrictive wins. AI Credits billing (since June 1, 2026): tool-definition token overhead directly increases per-interaction cost. MCP servers supported: local (stdio) and remote (SSE/HTTP). GitHub MCP Server (hosted) is directly available. MCP Registry at github.com/mcp lists available servers. Virtual tools threshold setting: github.copilot.chat.virtualTools.threshold (integer; setting >128 has no effect since API cap is 128). Copilot Studio skills limit (for agents built in Copilot Studio): 100 skills per agent. Connector payload for Copilot Studio: 5 MB (public cloud), 450 KB (GCC).

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

skills_supported.notes: MCP servers serve as the skills mechanism in GitHub Copilot. Each MCP server exposes tools that Copilot agent mode can invoke. The GitHub MCP server includes tools for GitHub API operations. Additional MCP servers from the GitHub MCP Registry can be added.

skills_loading_model.notes: All configured MCP server tools are loaded per session into the model context (always_on by default). With virtual tools enabled, large tool sets are deferred behind stubs (partial deferred loading). Tools from all connected servers are available in each turn subject to the 128-tool request cap.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: MCP server tool definitions are injected as input tokens for every turn in agent mode. With many servers/tools, this can consume a significant fraction of the context window before any user prompt or code context is added. GitHub community reports confirm rapid context fill-up with multiple MCP servers. The AI Credits billing model (June 2026+) means tool-definition token overhead directly affects per-interaction cost. Virtual tools feature (embedding-guided clustering) reduces token overhead by deferring non-core tools behind stubs.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: GitHub Copilot injects a system prompt per turn that includes IDE context (open files, cursor position, recent edits), repository context (if applicable), and MCP tool definitions. Total overhead not published. Community reports suggest ~40% of context window reserved for output.

Underlying GPT-5/Claude models support prompt caching in their APIs; whether GitHub passes this through is unclear.

detail.notes: MULTI-MODEL PRODUCT ENTRY: GitHub Copilot is a developer product (IDE + CLI + web) that exposes a model picker letting users choose from GPT-5 family (OpenAI), Claude family (Anthropic), Gemini family (Google), and MAI-Code-1 (Microsoft). Context window, tokenizer, and cost all depend on the selected model. MOST RELEVANT for MCP Token Footprint: GitHub Copilot natively supports MCP servers (GA in VS Code 1.99+) with a hard 128-tool cap at the VS Code client layer. MCP tool definitions are injected into the model context as input tokens and directly consume the context window. Virtual tools feature (embedding-guided clustering) defers large tool sets behind stubs to stay under the 128 limit. Default built-in toolset trimmed to 13 core tools (Nov 2025). Billing switched to AI Credits (per-token, model-dependent) on June 1, 2026. MAI-Code-1 is Microsoft's own inference-efficient coding model available in Copilot and VS Code (announced Build 2026).

Connector tool schemas are loaded into context when a Connector is referenced; large MCP servers with many tools will consume substantial context budget.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No API-enforced cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn. The Agents SDK defaults to 20 max_turns as a safety measure, but this is SDK-level, not API-enforced. Agentic loops run until the model returns a final message or context window is exhausted.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented hard cap on the number of remote MCP servers that can be connected. ChatGPT help doc confirms 'multiple first-party and third-party apps in a single prompt' are supported. The binding constraint is the 128-tool aggregate limit per request.

max_total_tools.notes: Same as max_tools_hard: 128 tools total per request regardless of how many MCP servers contribute tools. Tools from multiple connected servers all count toward this single 128-tool budget.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: JSON Schema for parameters follows OpenAI's structured outputs subset. Strict mode (strict:true) enforces: (1) additionalProperties must be false on all objects; (2) all properties must be listed in 'required'; (3) max 100 object properties total; (4) max 5 nesting levels; (5) anyOf supported only for nullable types (anyOf: [{type: X}, {type: null}]); (6) $ref not supported in strict mode; (7) oneOf/allOf have problems in strict mode; (8) keywords pattern, minLength, minimum, format are accepted but NOT enforced by the model. Non-strict mode accepts a broader subset. No documented byte-size limit on total tool definition payload beyond the context window.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Remote MCP (Responses API): tool definitions from MCP servers are fetched at request time, cached with the request, and billed as input tokens. allowed_tools parameter can filter which tools are exposed from a connected MCP server to reduce token overhead. ChatGPT MCP apps (Business/Enterprise): full MCP with write actions available in beta; no hard server-count cap documented but tools must fit within 128-tool budget. Deep research (ChatGPT product): MCP servers limited to read/fetch actions only. Rate limits: per-model RPM/TPM limits apply (see platform.openai.com/settings/limits); no tool-specific rate limits documented separately.

tokenizer_public.notes: No public tokenizer library, HF repo, or tiktoken base found. Console playground exists for interactive exploration but no programmatic access documented. No count_tokens API endpoint found. Medium confidence because absence of documentation does not guarantee no internal release.

tokenizer_access.notes: Access is limited to the interactive console Tokenizer Playground (https://console.x.ai). No API endpoint, no library. Closed for programmatic local use.

count_tokens_method.notes: No count_tokens API endpoint documented. Only option is the console Tokenizer Playground (interactive). For programmatic estimation, use raw_json_rough fallback or an approximate chars-per-token ratio.

image_token_rule.notes: grok-4.3 supports image input (modalities: Text, Image). Pricing docs mention 'Image tokens: Visual content analysis (when applicable)' as billed but no tile/patch conversion rule is published (unlike OpenAI's tile formula). Undocumented.

audio_token_rule.notes: grok-4.3 does not support audio input. Audio is handled by separate Voice API models.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Standard rough estimate of ~4 chars/token for English text with BPE-style tokenizers. No xAI-specific ratio published. Use raw_json_rough profile.

function_calling.notes: Full function calling supported. Uses OpenAI-compatible tool format in both Chat Completions and Responses API.

native_mcp.notes: Remote MCP Tools supported natively via Responses API and xAI SDK. Specify {type: 'mcp', server_url, server_label}. xAI manages the MCP connection server-side. Supports Streaming HTTP and SSE transports. Available November 2025 (GA).

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Parallel function calling enabled by default. Docs state: 'the model can request multiple tool calls in a single response.' Disable with parallel_tool_calls: false.

max_tools_hard.notes: Function calling schema reference table (verified June 2026): 'name — Unique identifier (max 200 tools per request)'. Applies to custom function tools passed in the tools array. The 200 cap is the documented API hard limit per request across all tool types (function + built-in). Confirmed on the live docs page last updated June 17, 2026.

max_tools_practical.notes: xAI docs themselves advise using allowed_tools to filter MCP tools to avoid context overhead: 'Reduce context overhead by limiting tool definitions the model needs to consider.' No empirical degradation study specific to Grok published. General community consensus ~30-50 tools before accuracy cliff (Berkeley FCL, Tier 4). Set to 40 as mid-range estimate.

tool_definition_shape.notes: xAI API is OpenAI-compatible. Function tools use {type: 'function', name, description, parameters} schema identical to OpenAI. Responses API also accepts OpenAI SDK directly via base_url override.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool definitions are injected into context and billed as input tokens. xAI docs for Remote MCP explicitly warn: 'all available tool definitions will be available to the model' and recommend using allowed_tools to 'Reduce context overhead.' Consistent with all OpenAI-compatible providers.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No tool search / deferred loading mechanism documented for xAI API. The allowed_tools parameter on Remote MCP can filter which tools are loaded, but this is a static list at request time, not progressive disclosure. No equivalent to Claude's ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH or defer_loading found.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No character limit on tool/function names documented in xAI docs. The schema reference lists 'name' as a required string field with no length constraint stated. Remote MCP tools are namespaced as '{server_label}.{tool_name}' in tool call output, but no total name-length constraint stated. Unlike OpenAI's 64-char limit, xAI publishes no equivalent constraint.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented cap on tool description length. The schema reference states 'description' is required ('What the tool does — helps the model decide when to use it') but specifies no character or token limit. Effectively bounded by the request's context window.

max_request_size.notes: No maximum request payload size (bytes/MB) published in xAI docs. Not found in function-calling docs, API reference, rate-limits page, or FAQ. Effectively bounded by the 1M token context window for this model.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented cap on tool result/output size. For server-side tools (web_search, MCP), tool outputs are consumed internally and not returned to the client by default. For client-side function tools, the result is returned as a string with no stated size limit — bounded by context window in practice.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: No documented cap on the number of parallel tool calls emitted in a single response. The docs state 'the model can request multiple tool calls in a single response' and 'process all of them before continuing' but give no numeric upper limit. Disable all parallel calling with parallel_tool_calls: false.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: The max_turns parameter controls server-side agentic loop turns (each turn = one model reasoning + one or more tool calls + tool results cycle). If max_turns is not specified, 'the server applies a global default cap' (exact number undisclosed). When the agent reaches the limit it stops calling tools and returns a final response. max_turns only applies within a single request; client-side tool calls act as checkpoints that reset the counter. The global default cap value is not published.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented cap on the number of simultaneous Remote MCP server connections per request. The Remote MCP docs show an example with 3 servers in a single request ('Multi-Server Support') with no stated limit: 'Enable multiple MCP servers simultaneously to create a rich ecosystem of specialized tools.' The only indirect constraint is that all tool definitions from all connected servers count toward the 200-tool hard limit and the context window.

max_total_tools.notes: No separate 'aggregate tools across servers' limit documented. The 200-tool per-request cap (from function calling docs) is the de-facto total ceiling when mixing function tools and MCP server tools in a single request.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Tool parameters root MUST be {"type": "object"}; a non-object root (scalar or array) causes a 400 error with the tool name identified in the error message. No documented depth, property count, or enum size limits beyond that constraint. Remote MCP tool names are namespaced as '{server_label}.{tool_name}' in responses (e.g., 'deepwiki.search_repository'). All tool definitions from connected MCP server(s) are injected into context automatically; use allowed_tools to filter. Max 200 tools per request hard limit applies to all tool types collectively. JSON Schema enums, anyOf, oneOf, $ref: not explicitly documented as unsupported but no examples use them; standard JSON Schema subset assumed.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Remote MCP: only Streaming HTTP and SSE transports supported (no stdio/STDIO). The OpenAI Responses API require_approval and connector_id parameters are NOT supported on xAI. xAI manages the MCP server connection server-side — no client-local MCP proxy required. For Voice Agent API, Remote MCP tools are also supported. Built-in server-side tools (web_search, x_search, code_execution) are billed per-call ($5/1k) plus token-based charges. Rate limits: 1,800 RPM / 10M TPM (Tier 0 defaults for us-east-1); see https://docs.x.ai/developers/rate-limits for per-tier table. The max_turns agentic loop parameter has an undisclosed server-enforced global default cap. Context Compaction (May 2026) can compact long agentic sessions automatically.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

skills_supported.notes: No API-level skills concept for grok-4.3. The Grok Build product has a Skills/Plugins/Marketplaces section but those are user-facing Grok Build CLI features, not developer API primitives that inject packaged context bundles.

skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: No fixed system-prompt overhead documented. System prompt tokens billed as input tokens at standard rate. Cached system prompt tokens billed at $0.20/1M (cached input rate).

prompt_caching.notes: Prompt caching is automatic for consecutive requests sharing the same starting messages. Cached tokens billed at $0.20/1M (vs $1.25/1M standard input). Use x-grok-conv-id header or prompt_cache_key to maximize cache hits. Released May 2025.

memory_feature.notes: No persistent memory feature documented for the API. Context Compaction (May 2026) allows shrinking long conversations but is not persistent memory. Grok consumer product may have memory features but not exposed in developer API.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard rate for requests up to 200K context. Higher context pricing applies above 200K (exact higher-context rate not published in scraped docs; model page notes 'We charge different rates for requests which exceed the 200K context window').

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cached input (prompt caching) rate: $0.20/1M. Listed as 'Cached input' in pricing table.

batch_discount.notes: Batch API applies 20%-50% off standard rates on all token types (input, output, cached, reasoning). Exact model-specific rate requires toggling 'Show batch API pricing' on model detail page. Processed asynchronously, typically within 24 hours.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image tokens billed as input tokens at standard rate when images are included in messages. No published tile/patch formula — exact per-image token cost requires testing. xAI pricing docs list 'Image tokens: Visual content analysis (when applicable)' as a standard billed token type.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Pricing docs: 'Reasoning tokens: Full completion token price.' Reasoning tokens tracked in completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens. Billed at $2.50/1M (same as output). Batch discount applies to reasoning tokens too.

detail.notes: grok-4.3 is xAI's current flagship model as of 2026-06-21. It absorbs a large number of legacy aliases (grok-3, grok-4, grok-4-fast, grok-3-mini, etc.) per the model detail page. The 'Grok 4 Fast ~2M context' referenced in some aggregators is NOT confirmed in current docs — the grok-4-fast alias now points to grok-4.3 with a 1M context window. Configurable reasoning (none/low/medium/high effort). Rate limit: 1,800 RPM, 10M TPM (us-east-1).

native_mcp.notes: Remote MCP tools supported: 'We do support a set of built-in tools (e.g., web_search, x_search) and remote MCP tools.' Client-side function calling is NOT supported; only server-side/MCP tools work.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Multiple agents execute in parallel, each capable of invoking built-in tools independently. Sub-agent tool calls billed separately.

max_tools_hard.notes: No explicit hard tool count limit documented for the multi-agent model. Only built-in server-side tools and Remote MCP tools are supported — custom function tools (which trigger the 200-cap) are not supported at all. The 200-tool limit from function-calling docs does not apply to this model variant. No separate documented limit on how many MCP tools can be loaded.

max_tools_practical.notes: No empirical data specific to multi-agent tool count degradation. Model uses server-side built-in tools only.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Uses OpenAI Responses API format: {type: 'web_search'}, {type: 'x_search'}, {type: 'mcp', server_url, server_label}. Client-side function calling shape (openai_function) is not supported for this model.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Remote MCP tool definitions injected into context and billed as input tokens. Built-in tools have per-call fees ($5/1k calls) plus token-based charges.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No deferred tool loading documented.

max_tool_name_len.notes: Not applicable for built-in tools; Remote MCP tool names inherited from server — no documented cap.

max_tool_description_len.notes: Not documented. Custom tool descriptions not applicable (function calling not supported). Remote MCP tool descriptions inherited from server.

max_request_size.notes: No maximum request payload size published. Only Responses API supported (no Chat Completions).

max_tool_result_size.notes: Server-side tool outputs (web_search, MCP) are consumed internally by agents and not returned to the client by default. Sub-agent state is encrypted. No documented output size cap.

context_window_tokens.notes: Model card states: 'Context Length: 262,144 natively'. Default serving context length. Shared input+output pool.

input_output_shared.notes: Standard transformer architecture; context window is a shared pool for input + output tokens combined.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived: context_window (262144) minus recommended max_output (81920). No hard vendor-published max_input cap; in practice the operator sets it via the serving framework.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Model card Best Practices recommends max_tokens=32768 for most queries.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Model card examples use max_tokens=81920 for complex problems; serving is set by operator via --max-model-len.

extended_context.notes: Model card states '262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,010,000 tokens' using YaRN RoPE scaling. Requires modifying rope_parameters in config.json or passing CLI overrides to vLLM/SGLang. Static YaRN may degrade short-text performance.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Qwen3.6 generates <think>...</think> reasoning blocks before the final response. These count toward output token budget and are billed as output tokens on DashScope.

tokenizer_family.notes: Qwen models use tiktoken-based BPE tokenization. The Qwen3 series shares the same tokenizer; vocabulary is 151,643 regular tokens + special/control tokens. Token embedding dimension uses padded 248320.

tokenizer_access.notes: Can be loaded via HuggingFace transformers AutoTokenizer. Underlying tokenizer uses tiktoken library with a custom vocabulary file. tokenizer.json available in HF repo.

count_tokens_method.value: from transformers import AutoTokenizer; tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B'); len(tok.encode(text))

image_token_rule.value: Variable tile-based patching; number of tokens depends on image resolution and model's visual encoder tiling
image_token_rule.notes: Qwen3.6 uses a vision encoder with tile-based patching. Exact per-pixel token count formula not published in model card; differs from Qwen-VL's documented tile formula. Use AutoProcessor to count multimodal tokens.

audio_token_rule.notes: Qwen3.6-27B does not natively support audio input (text+image+video). Audio is handled by separate Qwen3-Omni / Qwen3.5-Omni models.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Rough estimate for English text using tiktoken BPE. Chinese text yields higher token density (~1.5 chars/token). Use AutoTokenizer for accuracy.

function_calling.notes: Qwen3.6 has strong function calling. vLLM/SGLang require --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder flag for structured tool output parsing.

native_mcp.notes: Qwen-Agent (the official agentic framework) accepts MCP server configs via mcpServers key in the function_list. MCP tool definitions are translated to Qwen function-call format and injected as input tokens.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Qwen3 series supports parallel/multi-tool calls in a single turn via the OpenAI-compatible chat completions API. Confirmed by Qwen-Agent framework behavior.

max_tools_hard.notes: No hard API-enforced tool count cap documented for Qwen models. When self-hosted, the serving framework does not enforce a tool limit. Context window is the effective limit.

max_tools_practical.notes: No vendor-published empirical degradation point. Community consensus for capable models is ~30-50 tools before accuracy degrades; 40 is a conservative estimate. Qwen3.6's strong tool-use benchmarks (BFCL, MCPMark) suggest it may tolerate more than weaker models.

tool_definition_shape.notes: DashScope and self-hosted endpoints both use OpenAI-compatible chat completions API format. Tool definitions follow the OpenAI function-calling JSON schema. Qwen-Agent also supports a native Qwen tool format internally, but the OpenAI-compatible API path is standard for integrations.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool definitions are serialized into the request and billed as input tokens. DashScope pricing page confirms: charged for input tokens and output tokens per request.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No documented tool-search or deferred-loading mechanism in vLLM/SGLang/Qwen-Agent equivalent to Claude's ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH. Tools are injected in full at request time.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No documented character limit on tool names for Qwen models. Follows OpenAI function-call schema conventions.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: No documented schema-depth or per-tool-definition size limits. Practical limit is total input token budget. Qwen3.6 MCPMark benchmark score of 37.0 indicates reasonable performance with standard tool schemas.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No vendor cap; description counts against context window.

max_request_size.notes: No vendor byte cap; bounded by serving config (vLLM --max-model-len / --max-num-batched-tokens) and GPU memory.

max_tool_result_size.notes: Context-bound; tool results count against max_model_len.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Depends on the model chat-template tool-call parser; see parallel_tool_calls.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: Set by the agent host/framework, not the model.

max_connected_servers.notes: Client/agent-framework-defined (e.g. Cursor caps ~40 tools total).

max_total_tools.notes: No vendor cap. Effective ceiling ≈ (context_window − output headroom) ÷ avg tool-definition tokens, set by serving config. Client hosts may cap lower (Cursor ~40, Claude Desktop ~100).

tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Open-weight: the model API layer imposes NO tool count/size caps. Binding limits come from (1) the serving stack — vLLM/SGLang max_model_len, max_num_batched_tokens, GPU KV-cache; (2) the model chat-template tool-call parser (must match --tool-call-parser); (3) the agent host (Cursor ~40-tool cap, Claude Desktop ~100). vLLM's default context is often 16K which silently truncates tool calls — raise --max-model-len.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

native_mcp.notes: The MODEL does not speak MCP protocol natively. MCP is a transport-layer protocol; the model generates function-call syntax in the Llama tool format. MCP integration is done by the serving/agent layer (e.g., llama-stack agent framework, or a custom MCP-to-tool-call bridge). Callers using an OpenAI-compatible endpoint from vLLM/SGLang can route MCP tool definitions as OpenAI function-calling JSON.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Llama 4 models support parallel tool calls (unlike Llama 3 which did not). Confirmed by vLLM tool calling documentation.

max_tools_hard.notes: No hard API-enforced tool count limit documented for the model itself. The effective limit is set by the serving framework and the context window. Tool definitions are injected as input tokens and consume the context window.

max_tools_practical.notes: No published empirical degradation point for Llama 4 Scout specifically. Community consensus for large-context models typically sees degradation around 30-50 tools (Berkeley FCL). With a 10M context window, tool definition token consumption is much less of a concern; practical limit more likely governed by model attention accuracy on long tool lists.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No native deferred/lazy tool loading in the model or standard serving stack. Tool search/deferral is a feature of specific agent frameworks layered on top (e.g., llama-stack). The 10M context window makes tool footprint less critical than for smaller-window models.

max_request_size.notes: No vendor byte cap; bounded by serving config (vLLM --max-model-len / --max-num-batched-tokens) and GPU memory.

batch_discount.notes: No vendor batch pricing. Self-hosted batched inference (vLLM continuous batching) improves throughput/GPU utilization but no token-price discount.
